lines.text: Any ratio or product with a temperature in it ($E_\text{k} = \frac{3}{2}k_\text{B}T$, $\sigma T^{4}$, gas laws) → convert to kelvin first; a temperature change can stay in °C ({{lesson:2.1}})

Energy to warm, melt or boil something → split the journey at each phase change: $Q = mc\Delta T$ for each warming stage, $Q = mL$ for each change of phase at constant temperature, then add ({{lesson:2.2}})

Hot and cold bodies mixed in an insulated container → energy lost by the hot body = energy gained by the cold body, with each $\Delta T$ written as hotter minus colder; solve for the shared final temperature ({{lesson:2.2}})
Steady rate of energy through a wall, window or rod → $\frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t} = kA\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta x}$ using the size of $\Delta T$ and $\Delta x$ in metres ({{lesson:2.3}})

Star's temperature, luminosity, radius or distance → Wien's law gives $T$ from the peak wavelength, $b = \frac{L}{4\pi d^{2}}$ links $L$ and $d$, and $L = \sigma(4\pi R^{2})T^{4}$ links $L$, $R$ and $T$ ({{lesson:2.4}})

Planet's equilibrium temperature → set the absorbed intensity $(1 - \alpha)\frac{S}{4}$ equal to the emitted $e\sigma T^{4}$; with an atmosphere, balance the surface alone: absorbed solar + radiated down by the atmosphere = emitted ({{lesson:2.5}})

Fixed amount of gas moving between two states → $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$, cancelling what stays constant; moles, molecules or mass in one state → $PV = nRT = Nk_\text{B}T$ in Pa, m³ and K ({{lesson:2.7}}, {{lesson:2.8}})
Molecular speed from pressure and density → $P = \frac{1}{3}\rho v^{2}$ gives $v_\text{rms}$; internal energy of an ideal monatomic gas → $U = \frac{3}{2}nRT = \frac{3}{2}PV$ ({{lesson:2.8}})

Gas is heated, cooled, compressed or expands → write $Q$ (heat in), $W$ (work by the gas: $P\Delta V$, or the area under the P–V line when $P$ changes) and, for a monatomic ideal gas, $\Delta U = \frac{3}{2}nR\Delta T$, each with its sign, then use $Q = \Delta U + W$ ({{lesson:2.9}})

Heat transferred at a fixed temperature (melting, boiling, a large reservoir) → $\Delta S = \frac{\Delta Q}{T}$ with $T$ in kelvin and $\Delta Q$ signed; to test whether a process can happen, add the entropy changes of every body involved and check the total is not negative ({{lesson:2.10}})

Monatomic ideal gas compressed or expanded with no heat flow (insulated or very fast) → adiabatic: $P_1V_1^{\frac{5}{3}} = P_2V_2^{\frac{5}{3}}$ for the new $P$ or $V$, then $PV = nRT$ for the temperature, and $W = -\Delta U$ ({{lesson:2.11}})

Efficiency of an engine running round a gas cycle → $\eta = \frac{W}{Q_\text{h}}$, with $W$ the area enclosed on the P–V diagram and $Q_\text{h}$ the heat taken in on the stages where $Q > 0$ only; the most any engine can reach is $1 - \frac{T_\text{c}}{T_\text{h}}$, in kelvin ({{lesson:2.11}})

Resistance of a wire from its size, or after it is stretched or swapped for a thicker one → $R = \frac{\rho L}{A}$ with $A = \pi r^{2}$ in $\text{m}^{2}$; change one factor at a time, and the area goes as the diameter squared ({{lesson:2.13}})

Meter reading after a resistor, LDR or thermistor changes → follow the chain one link at a time: total resistance → current → pd across the fixed resistor ($IR$) or the lost volts ($Ir$) → reading; use $\varepsilon = I(R + r)$ when the cell has internal resistance ({{lesson:2.14}})
